verses.text: When David was old and had lived a long, full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
He gathered all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites.
The Levites who were thirty years old or older were counted. One by one, there were thirty-eight thousand men.
David said, "Twenty-four thousand of them will be in charge of the work of the LORD's temple. Six thousand will be officials and judges.
Four thousand will be gatekeepers, and four thousand will praise the LORD with the musical instruments I have made for praise."
David divided the Levites into groups based on the families of Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
From the Gershonites came Ladan and Shimei.
Ladan had three sons: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel.
Shimei had three sons: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. These were the heads of Ladan's families.
Shimei's sons were Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were Shimei's sons.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah was second. But Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted together as one family group with one assignment.
Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were set apart forever to make the most holy things holy, to burn incense before the LORD, to serve him, and to bless people in his name forever.
But the sons of Moses, the man of God, were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.
Gershom's descendants were led by Shebuel.
Eliezer's descendants were led by Rehabiah. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had very many sons.
Izhar's descendants were led by Shelomith.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
Uzziel's sons were Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without having sons. He had only daughters, and they married their cousins, the sons of Kish.
Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.

These were the descendants of Levi by their families, the heads of families as they were listed by name and counted one by one. They were twenty years old or older, and they did the work of serving in the LORD's temple.
David had said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.
So the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the objects used in its service."
Following David's last instructions, the Levites twenty years old or older were counted.

Their job was to help Aaron's descendants in the service of the LORD's temple. They took care of the courtyards and the side rooms, the cleansing of all the holy things, and other work in the service of God's temple.
They were in charge of the holy bread on the table, the fine flour for the grain offerings, the thin cakes made without yeast, the baking pans, the mixing, and all the measuring of amounts and sizes.
They were also to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and to do the same every evening.
They helped whenever burnt offerings were offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, New Moon festivals, and other appointed feasts. They served before the LORD regularly, in the numbers required by the rules.
So the Levites took care of the Tent of Meeting and the holy place, and they helped their relatives, Aaron's descendants, in the service of the LORD's temple.
